config.title: Berlin Pink Pipes - FAQ
config.subtitle: Straight answers about Berlin's temporary groundwater pipes and the permanent Rosa Röhre landmark.

items.q: What are the pink pipes in Berlin for?
items.a: Most coloured pipes on temporary supports beside a building site carry groundwater pumped out during construction. Berlin Water Works says the water is pumped away so crews can work dry at depth. Read the site context first rather than assuming the colour has one universal meaning.

items.q: Why are there so many above-ground pipes in Berlin?
items.a: Groundwater depth varies around Berlin, but it can be close to the surface in parts of the inner city. When an excavation reaches groundwater, a temporary above-ground line can move that water away while the work continues. Its route and destination depend on the individual project.

items.q: Do the pipe colours mean different things in Berlin?
items.a: Do not use paint colour as a citywide code. Berlin Water Works describes pipes in pink, blue and yellow for this type of construction groundwater work. A nearby dig, temporary supports and site barriers are stronger clues than the colour alone.

items.q: Is Berlin's Rosa Röhre a construction pipe?
items.a: No. Umlauftank 2, often called the Rosa Röhre, is a permanent pink tube built into a Technical University of Berlin hydraulic-engineering and shipbuilding research facility near the Landwehrkanal. It is architecture and research infrastructure, not a temporary excavation line.

items.q: Can I walk over a temporary pink pipe in Berlin?
items.a: Use a marked ramp only when the site provides one, and stay outside the barriers. Do not climb, sit on or lean on a pipe for a photograph. For any route change or access issue, follow the current site notice rather than a general explainer.
